title: unified-rollouts: staged shadow probing and robust auto-rollback improvements
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: We observed occasional instability when introducing shadow traffic at scale. Issues include transient metric spikes from cold caches and noisy signals from rare long-tail requests which caused premature auto-rollbacks during new model rollouts. This PR introduces a staged shadow probing mode, improved metric aggregation windows, and stronger safety gates for automated rollback policies to reduce noisy false positives while preserving quick detection of real regressions.

What this change does: 
- Adds a staged shadow probing workflow that gradually increases shadow traffic to a new model variant over a configurable probing window. The probe tracks both latency and quality metrics with separate warmup and steady-state windows.
- Improves metric aggregation logic used by the autorollback controller: uses weighted rolling windows, outlier trimming, and signal hysteresis to avoid reacting to single-sample anomalies.
- Introduces an explicit failure budget per rollout that prevents autorollback from triggering if a transient spike is below the configured budget.
- Adds e2e and unit tests for the new controllers, and an observability dashboard with example alert thresholds.

Design notes: 
- Staged probing is implemented as a new rollout phase (probe -> steady -> ramp) in the unified-rollouts controller. Probe phase sends configurable percentage of shadow traffic and requires both latency and quality signals to pass separate thresholds. After probe success, the controller proceeds to steady where traffic and metric windows widen.
- Metric aggregation was refactored into a small library (rollout-metrics) that supports multiple windowing strategies and trimming. This allows reuse between canary and shadow workflows.
- Failure budget is an additional field on RolloutSpec: failure_budget (percentage/time) and is enforced by the autorollback reconciler.

Checklist: 
- [x] Controller implementation for staged shadow probing
- [x] Metric aggregation library with tests
- [x] Autorollback safety gates and failure budget enforcement
- [x] Unit + integration tests covering probe->steady transitions
- [x] Observability: dashboards and example alert rules
- [x] Documentation updates (api + runbook)

Backward compatibility & migration: 
- The new rollout phase is optional; existing RolloutSpecs will continue to behave the same. If failure_budget is omitted, controller defaults to previous behavior. We added a gentle migration note in docs explaining the new fields and recommended defaults.

Performance impact: 
- The staged probing logic adds negligible CPU overhead to the controller loop; most changes are in control-plane logic and metric computation. E2E tests show no impact to serving latency.

Testing and CI: 
- Local unit tests: rollout-metrics (100% coverage on core aggregation functions).
- Integration tests: probe-to-steady + simulated noisy signals.
- Staging canary: we ran a running rollout in staging over 72 hours and observed autorollback rate drop by ~60% on synthetic noisy signals while maintaining detection of real regressions.

Related: ENG-8421 (staged shadow rollout), ENG-8490 (autorollback hysteresis), PRs: pr-192501, pr-176210 for previous autorollback work.
